THE PARLOUR / TAKE YOUR TIME

The Other Half

Cut a connected estate into two connected parcels, then opponent chooses first under asymmetric public utilities.

Restart this deal
Another deal

A THOUGHTFUL LITTLE MATCH

Find your next move.

Balance rival score-difference choices without equalizing parcel area or own utility, use shape constraints to deny a high-value bundle, decide which round merits redraw rather than accept an adverse division. When choosing, own immediate score competes with withholding opponent score because match is score difference.

Take a seat
How to play
Fixed connected 4×4 estate of terrain cells with public red/blue utility weights and one adjacency bonus per connected orchard pair. Across six rounds draw different estates and utility cards; players alternate divider/chooser. Divider selects subset; both parcels nonempty and orthogonally connected. Chooser freely selects either parcel, divider gets remainder. House chooser maximizes its own awarded utility minus opponent awarded utility, consistent with match score difference; human chooses freely. A player scores own utility only. Each has two once-per-match redraw tokens usable before division, replacing an estate at cost two points. All utilities and future two estate types visible. Only the divider may spend a redraw token, before touching the cut. The house may also redraw an unfavorable estate at a two-point cost; each side has two tokens.
Score difference over six rounds decides win/loss; equality draws. Invalid disconnected cut never commits.

Forty-eight tiles, twelve symbols four copies each, arranged on three explicit layers. Tile removable only if nothing covers it and left or right side has no tile at same layer. Select two removable identical tiles to remove together. No shuffle or arbitrary hint teleport; unlimited inspection and three undo credits per deal. Known tile faces always visible in a layer list.
